'''AaB''',<ref>[http://www.aabsport.dk/media/374097/2011__rsrapport_aab.pdf Årsrapport for 2011] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140723180916/http://www.aabsport.dk/media/374097/2011__rsrapport_aab.pdf |date=23 July 2014 }}, Aalborg Boldspilklub A/S, p.9</ref> (full name: ''Aalborg Boldspilklub'', {{IPA|da|ˈʌlˌpɒˀ ˈpʌlˀtspe̝lˌkʰlup|pron}}) internationally referred to commonly as '''Aalborg BK''',<ref>[https://www.uefa.com/nationalassociations/den/domestic/league/1031/ Denmark – Danish Super League]  UEFA.com</ref>  and occasionally referred to as '''AaB Aalborg''', is a professional [[association football|football club]] based in [[Aalborg]], Denmark. The club currently competes in the [[Danish 1st Division]], the second tier of Danish football. AaB is one of the oldest and most historically significant clubs in Danish football, having been founded on 13 May 1885. Initially formed as a cricket club by English railway engineers, the club adopted football in 1902 and has competed under the name ''Aalborg Boldspilklub af 1885'' since 1906.

AaB has traditionally been a mainstay in the Danish top flight, and has won the [[Danish Superliga]] four times, in [[1994–95 Danish Superliga|1994–95]], [[1998–99 Danish Superliga|1998–99]], [[2007–08 Danish Superliga|2007–08]], and [[2013–14 Danish Superliga|2013–14]]. The latter season remains the club's most successful, as AaB won [[Double (association football)|the domestic double]] by securing both the league title and the [[Danish Cup]]. In total, the club has lifted the national cup three times. After a period of decline in the early 2020s, AaB was relegated from the top tier at the end of the [[2022–23 Danish Superliga|2022–23 season]] for the first time in 36 years. The club secured immediate promotion in [[2023–24 Danish 1st Division|2023–24]] but was relegated again the following season, returning to the [[Danish 1st Division]] for the 2025–26 campaign.

On the European stage, AaB holds the distinction of being the first Danish club to reach the group stage of the [[UEFA Champions League]], doing so in [[1995–96 UEFA Champions League|1995–96]] after replacing [[FC Dynamo Kyiv|Dynamo Kyiv]], who were expelled for disciplinary reasons. The club later qualified directly for the group stage in [[2008–09 UEFA Champions League|2008–09]], and remains one of Denmark's most frequent participants in the competition, second only to [[F.C. Copenhagen]] in appearances."}}
